subject.title: [Feature]: Show session and requester context in macOS exec approval popup

question: Which requester context may the macOS exec-approval dialog disclose: session key only, normalized origin metadata such as channel and thread, or identifiable sender/account data?
rationale: The existing omission is clear, but sender and routing metadata are privacy-sensitive and the current Swift protocol model does not carry a reviewed disclosure contract.

options.title: Session plus normalized origin
options.body: Show the existing session key and a bounded channel/thread label when present, while excluding raw sender and account identifiers.

options.title: Session only
options.body: Land the smallest parity fix and defer all origin metadata until a separate disclosure design is approved.

options.title: Full requester identity
options.body: Expose sender/account details only after maintainers define the trust boundary, redaction rules, and compatibility behavior.

recommendation.title: Session plus normalized origin
recommendation.body: Show the existing session key and a bounded channel/thread label when present, while excluding raw sender and account identifiers.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly concerns the native macOS approval-presenter model and its user-facing disclosure boundary.
